title: Flix Canonical-Tree Transparency Contract
description: Schema for ast/transparency.json, the curated list of canonical TreeKinds that are removed when a projected tree is normalised. An entry is a claim about the *reference's own structure* -- this node contributes one edge and no leaf content, or it is a recovery marker rather than syntax -- and it must be argued with source citations. It is never a claim about any consumer: with one instrumented consumer, no automated check can tell a neutral rule from a consumer-shaped one, so the reasons are the only thing that can, and a reason naming a consumer is rejected on sight.

upstreamCommit.description: flix/flix commit every citation below was read against. Asserted against pin.json exactly as ast/unattachable.json is, so a pin bump fails until the evidence is re-verified rather than silently carrying stale line numbers.

note.description: Free-text maintenance note explaining the file's contract to a human editor.

treeKinds.description: Entries whose name must exist in ast/treekind.json, sorted by name and never repeated.

name.description: Qualified TreeKind name, matching ast/treekind.json exactly.

rule.description: `elide` removes the node when it has no children and replaces it with its single child when it has one; a node with two or more children is kept, because splicing it would discard real structure. `splice` lifts the node's children into its parent at any arity, which is stronger and is reserved for nodes that are not syntax at all.

recoveryMarker.description: True when the kind marks error recovery rather than syntax. Such a kind is spliced out of the canonical tree so the main lane measures structure *modulo* recovery, and its shape is measured instead by the recovery lane against fixtures/raw/. Recovery shape is implementation-specific by nature, which is why it is a separate lane rather than a separate score.

reason.description: Why the reference's own structure makes this node carry no information beyond its child, or makes it a recovery marker. Long enough to force an argument rather than an assertion. Must not name a consumer: 'parser X does not produce one' is evidence about X, not about the reference.

items.description: Upstream-relative path and line, read at upstreamCommit.

citations.description: Every site that closes this kind, so a reader can confirm the arity claim against the parser rather than against this file.
